rules.title: Civil Code section 1950.6 (Application screening fees)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge an application screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs and the reasonable value of time, capped at $30 per applicant (CPI-adjustable annually since 1998). No fee may be charged when no unit is available, and the landlord must offer first-come-first-served screening or refund fees to unselected applicants, give an itemized receipt, return unused amounts, and provide a copy of the credit report within seven days.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI from Jan 1, 1998
rules.status_basis: Section is in the California Civil Code (updated Jan. 1, 2026).

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants.

precedence.text: This section is not intended to preempt any provisions or regulations that govern the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
